title: Stakeholder priority lens: Observability scope + agenda
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic working agenda to converge stakeholders (product, support, SRE, serving-runtime, and solutions) on a small set of high-impact observability initiatives for H1. Focus: reduce investigation time for token-path latency, remove noisy panels, and establish a repeatable decision lens for future dashboard requests.

Intended audience: product PMs, oncall leads, ops owners, and observability engineers.

Meeting objective (60 minutes):
- Align on 3 prioritized workstreams and their measurable outcomes.
- Agree a lightweight scoring rubric for metric/dashboard requests.
- Assign owners and a 6-week delivery runway for the first tranche.

Attendees (suggested):
- Sofia Patel (obs lead) — facilitator
- Marcus Li (serving-runtime) — infra constraints + instrumentation readiness
- Ava Chen (product-hosted-api) — user impact & SLO lens
- Diego Morales (oncall) — operator friction & triage time data
- 1x CS/solutions rep for customer-facing pain points

Quick background (why now):
- Oncall investigations for token spikes currently average ~47 minutes; several repeated dashboards offer little signal.
- There is an incoming dedicated capacity launch that will change latency distributions; need targeted probes and fewer, higher-fidelity panels.

Proposed 3 priority workstreams (high level):
1) Investigation-first dashboard condensation
   - Goal: reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for token-latency incidents by 30% for top 3 tenants.
   - Deliverables: 1 compact incident play dash, 2 micro-probes (cold-kv-warmth, prefix-heatmap), runbook sample queries.
   - Owner: Diego Morales; Support: Marcus Li; ETA: 5 weeks.

2) Metric contract audit + retires
   - Goal: prune 25% of high-cost panels and stabilize remaining metrics with clear derivations.
   - Deliverables: metric-contract doc for top 50 metrics, deprecation list, sample queries for validation, cost estimate delta.
   - Owner: Sofia Patel; Support: observability devs; ETA: 6 weeks.

3) Tracing policy for fanout & multi-model routing
   - Goal: ensure traces have consistent anchors for session context across model routing and fallback flows.
   - Deliverables: trace-span taxonomy, minimal sampling rules for fallback severity, example trace annotations for tool-calls and cache hits.
   - Owner: Marcus Li; Support: SRE, runtime team; ETA: 4 weeks.

Decision lens (scoring rubric) — use this to accept/reject dashboard/metric requests:
- User Impact (0–5): how many internal/external users impacted; link to customer incidents.
- Investigation ROI (0–5): time recovered in oncall investigations per month.
- Query Cost (0–5, inverted): expected query cost increase to metrics infra.
- Implementation effort (0–5, inverted): dev time to instrument/validate.
- Long-term reusability (0–5): likely to be reused for future rollouts or other tenants.

Accept if: WeightedScore >= 12 (weights: UserImpact*1.5 + InvestigationROI*1.3 + Reusability*1.0 - QueryCost*0.9 - Effort*0.8).
(We will keep the formula in the prioritization spreadsheet and re-evaluate after the first triage cycle.)

Dashboard recipe examples (compact, operator-first):
- Incident play dash (single column layout):
   1) Top line: tenant SLO / 1m quantile latency / token-rate trend (-> show release spikes)
   2) Microprobe tiles: KV-warmth index, prefix-hit-rate, model-loads-per-minute
   3) Trace anchor: sample trace links with span id mapping (one-click drilldown)
   4) Query cost indicator + last-refresh timestamp

- Cost-lite model rollout dashboard:
   1) Per-model tail latency 95/99 -> compare quantized vs float model variants
   2) Token-economics panel: tokens served per second, tokens per request distribution
   3) Fallback rate vs capacity tier (hosted/dedicated/private)

Tracing/annotation conventions (proposal):
- session_id: 1 per API request; must be preserved across routing and fanout.
- route_key: identifies routing policy used (e.g., low-latency-fallback, cost-saver)
- model_variant: short name (e.g., rwkv-13b-q4f)
- kv_cache_hit: boolean span attribute when prefix/KV returned a hit
- fallback_reason: if fallback occurs, include code (CAPACITY, DEGRADED_QUALITY, TIMEOUT)
- sample_rate tagging: traces with fallback_reason != null -> sample_rate=1.0 (always capture).

Sampling policy (practical):
- Baseline traces: 0.5% global for production.
- High-value buckets: always sample (100%) if fallback_reason present or if request latency > 99th percentile for that tenant.
- Developer test projects: 5% (easier to correlate functional issues).

Acceptance criteria for rollouts (short checklist):
- Dashboards: compact dash validated against synthetic incidents and one historical incident replay.
- Metrics: contract doc signed off by metric owner; low-cardinality tags reviewed.
- Traces: sample coverage validated for fallback flows for top 10 tenants.

Quick timeline & milestones (6-week view):
- Week 0: Triage meeting (use this doc) -> agree owners & scoring on 2026-02-10
- Week 1–2: Metric contract audit + initial dashboard wireframes
- Week 3: Tracing taxonomy draft + sampling experiments in staging
- Week 4–5: Implement micro-probes and validation queries; operator dry-run
- Week 6: Launch compact dashes + postmortem for the triage cycle; measure MTTR delta

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: high query cost from new microprobes -> Mitigation: budget probe queries behind a feature flag and measure incremental cost for 2 weeks.
- Risk: sampling or trace annotation drift -> Mitigation: small static schema with lint checks in CI and a telemetry alert when expected keys disappear.
- Risk: stakeholder disagreement on retirements -> Mitigation: mandatory 2-week announcement + backup snapshot of dashboard JSON.

Open questions for the triage meeting:
- What tenant list do we run the first MTTR measurement on? (propose top 3 by monthly tokens)
- Which oncall rotations should be part of the dry-run? (night + day primary)
- Do we enable always-sample fallback traces for Private deployments by default? (privacy/PII concern)

Action items (post-meeting):
- Sofia: publish prioritized list + spreadsheet with scoring columns (due 2026-02-12).
- Marcus: prototype span template and a staging trace example (due 2026-02-17).
- Diego: pick two historical incidents and run dashboard dry-run (due 2026-02-19).

Notes to self / brass-tacks: keep the first tranche narrow. We only get traction if we ship visible operator wins (faster incident resolution, fewer dashboard panels). Resist building "one-more-global-surface".

Appendix: quick scoring example (toy):
- Request: new "prefix-warmth" panel for tenant Acme Inc.
- Scores: UserImpact=4, InvestigationROI=5, QueryCost=2, Effort=2, Reusability=4 -> Weighted = 4*1.5 + 5*1.3 + 4*1.0 - 2*0.9 - 2*0.8 = 6 + 6.5 + 4 -1.8 -1.6 = 13.1 -> Accept.

End.
